result.topic_en: Euler examines the limiting case gg = fh, where the two parabolic solutions coincide and give the longest throw, and explains the paradox that the broken path FfhH has a smaller 'momentum' than the parabolic arc, noting that the calculus still covers this case because the vertical lines satisfy the differential condition.

§. 15. Ad haec paradoxa explicanda notari oportet
momentum viae $\mathrm{F}fh\mathrm{H}$ respondens etiam in suo ge-
nere esse minimum. Scilicet si puncta $f$ et $h$ aliquantum
mutentur, momentum, quod respondet viae $\mathrm{F}f'h'\mathrm{H}$ mani-
